comparisons.peer_summary: AMD develops world-class software stacks, including tools, compilers, and drivers, and works with customers to define customized solutions using its IP and design leadership.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVIDIA and AMD describe their foundational strategy of developing comprehensive software stacks to support their hardware. NVIDIA emphasizes its computer graphics platforms leveraging AI end-to-end, including developer tools and cloud services, while AMD explicitly lists its software stacks as including 'development tools, compilers, and drivers' for its products. Both companies frame these software ecosystems as critical components of their business strategy alongside their hardware IP.

sentences.text: Our computer graphics platforms leverage AI end-to-end, from the developer tools and cloud services to the Tensor Cores included in all RTX-class GPUs.
Our software stacks include development tools, compilers, and drivers for our CPUs, APUs, GPUs and FPGAs.

comparisons.peer_summary: The AMD Radeon PRO family provides professional graphics products optimized for demanding use cases such as 3D rendering, CAD, and media/entertainment pipelines on high-resolution displays.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose specific professional graphics product families targeting design and creative industries. NVIDIA identifies the 'geometric, design, and creative industries' as key drivers served by its GeForce and NVIDIA RTX platforms, whereas AMD details its 'AMD Radeon PRO family of professional graphics products' optimized for 'design and manufacturing for Computer-Aided Design (CAD), and media and entertainment.' Both use their professional GPU lines to address the same vertical markets.

sentences.text: Our technologies are instrumental in driving the gaming, design, and creative industries forward, as developers leverage our libraries and algorithms to deliver an optimized experience on our GeForce and NVIDIA RTX platforms.

Our AMD Radeon PRO family of professional graphics products are designed for integration in desktop workstations, optimized through hardware and software for demanding use cases such as 3D rendering, design and manufacturing for Computer-Aided Design (CAD), and media and entertainment for broadcast and animation pipelines on high resolution displays.
